scenes.name: EP 1 · EXT. DEV'S TERRACE — NIGHT
scenes.summary: string lights, ring light glow, quiet rooftop above the city

shots.action: Establisher: the terrace at night, string lights strung along the railing, a ring light glowing on its stand. Traffic hum below.
Master two-shot: Maya crouched by the phone rig checking the frame, Dev cross-legged behind her shuffling a stack of handwritten cue cards.
MAYA, holding up a cue card, dead serious.
shots.dialogue: Okay. Card six. Worst one we've got.

shots.action: DEV, flat.
shots.dialogue: We agreed no ranking mid-shoot.

shots.action: Maya, unbothered, already turning the card around.
shots.dialogue: I'm not ranking. I'm forecasting.

shots.action: Dev pinches the bridge of his nose, phone forgotten in his other hand.
shots.dialogue: That's the same thing with extra syllables.

shots.action: Insert: the cue card, corner curling from three nights of rehearsal.
Maya, reading it straight-faced.
shots.dialogue: Are you a parking ticket? Because you've got fine written all over you.

shots.action: Dev, staring at her, unmoved.
shots.dialogue: Nobody has said that out loud since 2009.

shots.action: Maya leans toward the lens, delighted with herself.
shots.dialogue: It's a classic. Classics don't die.

shots.action: Dev, instantly.
shots.dialogue: This channel might, if we keep using it.

shots.action: Maya sets the card down, suddenly serious in a different way, turns to actually face him.
Dev notices the shift, half-smiles, wary.
Maya, quieter.
shots.dialogue: Okay, real question. Off-camera voice, camera's still rolling though.

shots.action: Dev, caught off guard, sets the cue cards down slowly.
shots.dialogue: That's not how off-camera works.

shots.action: Maya, already asking anyway.
shots.dialogue: If we hadn't started this stupid channel, would you still be my best friend?

shots.action: Dev, actually thinking about it, which is its own answer.
Maya watching him think, the joke gone out of her face entirely.
Dev, finally.
shots.dialogue: Obviously.

shots.action: Wide on the terrace: the ring light still glowing, the two of them just sitting in it, the cue cards forgotten between them.
Superimposed caption card: KEEP THE TAKE — Episode One FADE OUT

scenes.name: EP 2 · EXT. COLLEGE GROUND — EVENING
scenes.summary: golden hour, open ground, a scooter parked where it shouldn't be

shots.action: New location, college ground at evening, golden light. Maya sets up the tripod at the edge of the running track.
Maya checks the framing on her phone, gives a thumbs-up toward off-frame.
A scooter rounds the corner of the ground, engine revving harder than a scooter needs to.
Dev's entrance, helmet under one arm, walking it like a red carpet. Slow motion, dramatic score sting.
Wider reveal: the scooter behind him is parked dead centre of the running track. He hasn't noticed.
SECURITY GUARD jogs in from the side, waving both arms.
shots.dialogue: Beta scooter hataao, coach ka round aane wala hai.

shots.action: Dev's entrance completely deflates mid-stride.
Maya, behind the tripod, already laughing, unable to hold the frame steady.
She gestures for him to just go move it.
shots.dialogue: Go, go, I'll cut around it.

shots.action: MATCH CUT on the clap →
Match-cut landing: the garage studio, egg-crate foam on the walls, a mic stand, both now seated across a small table.
Maya.
shots.dialogue: Okay. Scene two. Camera's rolling.

shots.action: Dev snaps into the bit, produces a paper flower from behind his back.
shots.dialogue: For you. I made it out of last month's electricity bill.

shots.action: Maya, flat.
shots.dialogue: That's not romantic, that's a fire hazard.

shots.action: Dev, wounded, staying in character.
shots.dialogue: Don't break the bit.

shots.action: Maya, not having it, phone buzzing in her pocket.
shots.dialogue: Dev.

shots.action: She checks the phone instead of the camera. Her face changes.
Dev, still holding the paper flower, watching her go somewhere he can't follow.
shots.dialogue: What.

shots.action: She turns the phone screen toward him. A confirmation email, subject line visible in frame.
Dev, caught.
shots.dialogue: That was supposed to be a maybe.
keyMoments: "That was supposed to be a maybe."

shots.action: Maya, quiet, the joke completely gone.
shots.dialogue: You interviewed. On a Tuesday. You told me you had a dentist thing.

shots.action: Dev stands, paper flower forgotten on the table.
shots.dialogue: I didn't want to make it a whole thing before I even knew.

shots.action: Maya, sharp.
shots.dialogue: It became a whole thing the second you sat across from someone and didn't call me.

shots.action: Dev paces to the mic stand and back, agitated.
shots.dialogue: I was going to tell you once it was real.

shots.action: Maya stands too, gathering the cue cards off the table without looking at them.
Maya.
shots.dialogue: It's been real for three weeks. I checked the email header.

shots.action: Dev, quiet.
shots.dialogue: Maya.

shots.action: Maya, imitating his earlier line, dead serious now.
shots.dialogue: Don't break the bit, right?

shots.action: Dev has nothing to say to that. Beat. He looks at the paper flower instead of her.
Maya, quieter, already packing the tripod.
shots.dialogue: Just tell me next time. That's all I ever ask.

shots.action: Both leave through opposite doors of the garage, the paper flower left alone on the table.
Superimposed caption card: KEEP THE TAKE — Episode Three FADE OUT

scenes.name: EP 4 · EXT. MAYA'S HOME STREET — MORNING
scenes.summary: hard morning light, quiet residential street

shots.action: Quiet residential street, morning light long across the road. A scooter pulls up.
Dev parking, RIA riding pillion, hopping off with a tripod bag slung over one shoulder.
keyMoments: Ria hops off with tripod bag

shots.action: He glances up at a first-floor balcony. Reveal: it's MAYA'S balcony, curtains still drawn.
Dev checks his phone, no reply to his last three messages, then the balcony again.
Dev briefing Ria in a low, hurried voice.
shots.dialogue: I just need five minutes of her actually listening. That's it.

shots.action: Ria, unpacking the tripod, dry.
shots.dialogue: You could've just called.

shots.action: They wait. Beat. Movement on the balcony above.
MAYA steps out with her coffee — her ordinary morning, no idea what's below.
Dev clocks her instantly, straightens up.
shots.dialogue: There.

shots.action: Ria, hoisting the tripod onto her shoulder, businesslike.
shots.dialogue: Camera's up whenever you are.

shots.action: Dev, a beat too late, nerves showing.
shots.dialogue: Okay. Okay, go.

shots.action: Ria lifts the camera to her eye, businesslike and quick — a total stranger to Maya from this distance.
Maya freezes mid-sip. Confusion tightening into something else in under two seconds.
She sets the coffee down hard enough that it slops over, storms back inside without a word.
Dev, still holding up a hand mid-wave, no one left to wave at.
Beat of dread on Dev. He looks at Ria.
Ria, already lowering the camera.
shots.dialogue: That didn't look like listening.

shots.action: MAYA comes out of the building gate fast, still in her pyjamas, phone in hand like evidence.
Dev, hands up before she's even said anything.
shots.dialogue: It's not what it looks like.

shots.action: Maya.
shots.dialogue: You brought a whole crew? To replace me you needed a crew?
keyMoments: "To replace me you needed a crew?"

shots.action: Dev, eyeing the tripod like it's suddenly a liability.
shots.dialogue: Ria's not — this isn't a replacement shoot.

shots.action: Maya.
shots.dialogue: Then what is it, Dev? Because from up there it looked exactly like a replacement shoot.

shots.action: Ria, stepping in, hand raised.
shots.dialogue: I'm his junior from the internship. I hold tripods for a living. That's the whole résumé.

shots.action: Maya stops mid-sentence, some of the fury draining out, replaced by confusion.
Maya, quieter but still raw.
shots.dialogue: Then why is there a camera at all, at seven in the morning?

shots.action: Dev, out of moves, just says it.
shots.dialogue: Because I couldn't figure out how to tell you the real thing without one running.

shots.action: Maya.
shots.dialogue: Tell me what real thing.

shots.action: Dev.
shots.dialogue: I took the job. I leave in nine days.

shots.action: Maya, still. Something deflates — anger draining into something rawer.
Maya.
shots.dialogue: Nine days. And you were going to make a video about it before you told me in person.

shots.action: Dev misreads the stillness as her being fine with it, relief flashing across his face.
Dev, relieved.
shots.dialogue: Right? I figured a proper episode would say it better than I could.

shots.action: Maya just looks at him. Eyes well up — not anger anymore. Hold.
She shakes her head slowly.
shots.dialogue: Nothing says it better than you actually saying it.

shots.action: The words land. Dev's face changes completely — realisation, too late, as always.
Dev.
shots.dialogue: Yeah.

shots.action: Superimposed caption card: KEEP THE TAKE — Episode Four FADE OUT

scenes.name: EP 5 · EXT. RIVERFRONT PROMENADE — NIGHT
scenes.summary: dim lamp posts, water reflections, warm pools in cold dark

shots.action: Quiet promenade, dim lamp posts, river reflections. Maya alone at the railing, staring at the water.
Maya in profile, unmoving.
Dev walks in carrying two takeaway cups.
Dev.
shots.dialogue: Figured you'd be here. You always come here when you're done being mad at me.

shots.action: Nothing from her.
Dev, again.
shots.dialogue: Maya.

shots.action: Softer, trying to coax a reaction. Lifts one cup.
shots.dialogue: It's the cheap chai. Your favourite kind of bad.

shots.action: Maya walks away down the promenade; Dev rushes after her.
Dev.
shots.dialogue: Maya, please, just say something.

shots.action: Maya, finally, sharp.
shots.dialogue: You had nine days of chances and you used all of them on a script.
keyMoments: "...you used all of them on a script."

shots.action: It actually stings.
shots.dialogue: I didn't know how else to get through it without falling apart in front of you.

shots.action: Maya turns to argue.
Maya.
shots.dialogue: So instead you got Ria to film it, so it could be neat. Edited.

shots.action: Dev, instant, easy.
shots.dialogue: Because you deserved neat. You didn't deserve me crying into a mic stand.

shots.action: Maya shakes her head.
shots.dialogue: I deserved you telling me. Messy is fine. Messy is us.

shots.action: He opens his mouth. Nothing comes out.
Maya keeps walking, slower now, not really trying to lose him.
Dev calls after her — defensive, deflecting first.
shots.dialogue: What do you want me to say, that the channel doesn't work without you? That I don't work without you?

shots.action: Maya stops. Looks at him properly for the first time all night. The turn — she starts listening. THE SPEECH — 5.20 to 5.33.
Dev, quiet. Drops the defence. Movement 1 — the admission.
shots.dialogue: I applied to that job the week my dad got sick again. I panicked and I didn't want it to be real until it had to be.

shots.action: Maya, listening. Not softened yet.
Movement 2 — the memory. He's half-smiling at it despite himself.
shots.dialogue: First video we ever posted, you made me redo the intro nineteen times. I still know it word for word. Nineteen.
keyMoments: "...I still know it word for word."

shots.action: Insert: his hands, absently miming the old intro gesture.
Two-shot. The physical distance between them, still not closed.
Movement 3 — the inventory. The small production things. This is where it stops being a speech.
shots.dialogue: You know my shot list before I write it. You know which take I'll pick before I pick it. I don't know how to make anything without you calling it first.

shots.action: Maya. Something behind her eyes changes.
His voice catches. He's not performing anymore — the first unscripted thing he's said all night.
Insert: he sets both cups down on the railing, hands finally free.
Her eyes await.
Movement 4 — the reframe. He answers a question she didn't ask.
shots.dialogue: I kept thinking the question was how do I leave without it ending us. Wrong question. The question is who I even am on a set without you next to me.

shots.action: Maya, mid-speech. Eyes going.
The landing.
shots.dialogue: Nine days isn't enough to fix five years of being bad at this. But I'd rather be bad at it in front of you than good at it anywhere else.

shots.action: The real line, thrown away quietly.
shots.dialogue: (beat) You're not losing your co-host. You're just getting a worse one, long-distance.

shots.action: Maya says nothing for a long moment. Her eyes are wet — this time it isn't anger.
Dev panics at his own sincerity and undercuts it.
shots.dialogue: Too much? That was too much, wasn't it. Delete that whole take.

shots.action: Maya, barely audible.
shots.dialogue: No. Keep it. Keep all of it. That's the first honest thing you've said in nine days.

shots.action: She leans in; Dev leans in assuming a hug — she grabs the spare battery pack out of his jacket pocket instead.
Maya, battery pack in hand, delighted with herself.
shots.dialogue: Camera's been on ninety percent for ten minutes. Someone has to think about b-roll.

shots.action: Dev looks at her, disappointed.
Maya laughs, then finally hugs him properly, battery pack still in her fist against his back.
Maya over his shoulder, meaning it this time.
shots.dialogue: I'm really going to miss you, idiot.

shots.action: Dev.
shots.dialogue: Only nine days left to prove it.

shots.action: Both laugh.
Maya, already scheming.
shots.dialogue: New segment. Long-distance co-host. I've got a whiteboard at home.

shots.action: Dev, seriously alarmed, throws up his hands.
Camera pulls back and up off the promenade; the two of them shrink into the string of riverside lights. Their banter continues as VO, score swells.
Superimposed caption card: KEEP THE TAKE — Episode Five FADE OUT PRODUCTION SUMMARY EP EPISODE LOCATION TIME SHOTS CAST KEY REQUIREMENTS 1 1 TERRACE
shots.dialogue: Don't break the bit
